Subject: Quick follow-up & next steps (SOC 2, KMS)

Hi Jake / Maya —

Thanks again for taking the time today — it was great to walk through how Redwood can help Acme reduce inference costs while meeting your security and compliance needs. Per our conversation, I wanted to recap the key security items you asked about and propose next steps.

Recap of asks from today:
- SOC 2: status and whether we can provide a redacted report
- Data classification / GDPR / HIPAA applicability
- Encryption: at-rest and in-transit defaults, and options for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)
- Vendor security questionnaire: you mentioned sending over a spreadsheet for us to fill

What I’m attaching: Redwood-Security-Overview.pdf (high-level controls) and a redacted SOC 2 Type II report (SOC2-TypeII-redacted.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
1) I will share the redacted SOC 2 report and the security overview (attached).
2) Please send the vendor security questionnaire (we can start filling it now) or confirm if the spreadsheet you referenced is the one titled "Vendor Security Questionnaire-ACME.xlsx" (if so, we have it on our side now).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with our security engineer (Aditya) to go into KMS/HSM details and encryption key lifecycle (30-45 min). Suggested times: Wed 3/18 10:00-10:45am PT or Thu 3/19 1:00-1:45pm PT.
4) If HIPAA will apply, let us know and we can run through available BAA options and data flow diagrams.

Short answers to the encryption questions you raised today:
- At-rest: All customer data stored by Redwood is encrypted at-rest using AES-256. For hosted customers we use provider-managed disk encryption by default, and we offer customer-managed key options (KMS) for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3 between client <> API and between internal service-to-service traffic.
- Customer-managed keys: We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault). For on-prem / air-gapped deployments we can integrate with HSM-backed KMS.

I'll coordinate the calendar once you confirm which time works best. If you'd like Aditya to include a short demo on how key rotation and re-encryption are handled in Dedicated, we can add that to the agenda.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Jake / Maya — thanks for the quick reply and for sending the questionnaire.

Answers inline to your numbered questions:
1) Key material: Redwood never persistently stores raw key material. For cloud KMS integrations we use envelope encryption: customer data keys are generated and wrapped by the cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault). The wrapped data keys are stored by Redwood; unwrapped key material is not exported by our services. If you need HSM-backed key operations, we can arrange a Dedicated/Private deployment with HSM integrations where key operations are performed inside your HSM and Redwood holds only wrapped keys/cryptographic references. Aditya, can you confirm we'd plan to demo the envelope encryption flow and key rotation timeline?

2) SOC 2 / subservice orgs: Attached is a short export that lists the main subservice providers (cloud infra, monitoring, logging, identity provider) used for controls. If procurement needs more detail we can provide vendor contact points and scoping.

3) BAA: We offer BAAs for Dedicated and Private customers today. For hosted customers we are evaluating a limited BAA offering in pilot; we can discuss interim mitigations (data segregation, logging, and contractual commitments) while you evaluate Dedicated/Private. If HIPAA is a firm requirement, we typically recommend Dedicated or Private so we can restrict data flows and sign a BAA.

Next steps:
- Aditya will join the technical deep-dive and cover envelope encryption, KMS integrations, and HSM options (we'll propose Wed 3/18 10:00am PT).
- I'll start filling the Vendor-Security-Questionnaire-ACME.xlsx and aim to return a draft within 48 hours; if there are any items that need technical details we'll flag them for Aditya to cover in the deep-dive.
- I'll also send a brief vendor/subservice export attachment.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Marissa
